title: Sheaf-valued supported kernel and supported closed inverse image
statement: Let $X,O,Z$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], $j:O\to X$ and $i:Z\to X$ morphisms. On abelian sheaves on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] and [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], use the inverse and direct image functors [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] and [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] and their canonical adjunction unit $\eta_j:1\to j_*j^{-1}$. Define $P_j=\ker(\eta_j)$ in the functor category, using sectionwise kernels [def-pur-abelian-sheaf-kernel], and define $i^!_{0,j}=i^{-1}P_j$. For a closed immersion $i$ and its complementary open immersion $j$, $P_j(F)$ is the subsheaf of sections supported on $Z$, viewed on $X$, and $i^!_{0,j}F$ is that supported sheaf viewed on $Z$. No exactness or adjunction property is included in this definition.

lean.note: §1(B) repair requested in the return of 3977feaf3409: the former supportedKernel/supportedClosedInverseImage attachment is specialized to AddCommGrpCat and cannot supply the module-valued support functor used by this consumer. The existing upstream sectionsWithSupport is the pointwise kernel of the canonical open unit and closedUpperShriek is this kernel followed by upperStar i, for an arbitrary Grothendieck abelian coefficient category A. Specializing A to AddCommGrpCat gives exactly this node, including arbitrary i and j; specializing to ModuleCat supplies the same construction over constant coefficients. The functor-category kernel is computed pointwise, so this is the same notion, not a new definition. The source section binds (A : Type u') [Category.{u + 1} A] [Abelian A] [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{u + 1} A] {Z U X : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X) (j : U ⟶ X).
